newsitem.title: USA: Stone Container to cut pulp, paper production.
newsitem.headline: Stone Container to cut pulp, paper production.

text.p: Stone Container Corp. said Friday it would cut production of pulp and paper after the world's leading producer of paperboard and paper packaging reported a $96.7 million first-quarter loss due to industrywide overproduction.
The Chicago-based company said it would reduce pulp and paper production by at least 350,000 tons through downtime at its pulp and paper mills.
Stone Container late Thursday reported a net loss equal to 99 cents a share, compared with a profit of $32.4 million, or 31 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996.

The loss, which the company attributed to low prices for its core products due to overproduction, fell below the consensus Wall Street analyst forecast of 93 cents a share, according to the First Call service.
Sales fell to $1.2 billion from $1.3 billion in the same period last year.
The cut in production comes on top of a 97,000-ton reduction in output that was put into effect in the first quarter, Stone Container said.
Company Chairman Roger Stone said he forsees a return to more normal market conditions as early as this summer.
Stone Container stock was unchanged at $10 a share in consolidated early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
